cards.front: The main weight-bearing bone of the leg is the [___].
cards.context: The tibia is the larger medial leg bone and forms the main load-bearing column. The fibula has a different primary role in stability and muscle attachment.

cards.front: Identify structure A in this distal wrist section. [___]
cards.context: Compression here causes carpal tunnel syndrome.

reference.title: Gray plate 422: transverse section of the wrist

cards.front: What are the seven bones between the leg and metatarsals called? [___]
cards.context: The tarsals form a three-dimensional platform between the leg and metatarsals. Their arrangement supports arches and adapts to the ground.

cards.front: Identify structure A in this distal wrist section. [___]
cards.context: Its palmar hook provides an ulnar attachment for the tunnel roof.

reference.title: Gray plate 422: transverse section of the wrist

cards.front: The nerve marked A supplies the [___] muscle.
cards.context: CN VI supplies lateral rectus. The nearby optic nerve has a different role: carrying visual information rather than moving the eye.

reference.title: Cranial Nerves III, IV, and VI: Oculomotor Function

cards.front: To test the superior oblique, ask the patient to adduct the eye and then [___] it.
cards.context: The superior oblique depresses the eye most effectively when the eye is already adducted. This emphasises its action relative to the vertical recti during examination.

reference.title: NCBI Bookshelf: ocular motor anatomy and palsy

cards.front: Which forearm bone lies on the side of digit five? [___]
cards.context: In standard anatomical position, the ulna is medial in the forearm, on the little-finger side.
